post.description:
Create an account. Students use their case.edu email and get a code to enter at POST /auth/verify;
alumni sign up with an invite from a member. Then sign in with POST /auth/login.

delete.description: Delete the account for good. The body must repeat the account's email address.

patch.description: Set or change the member's first or last name. Their book shows the new name straight away.

get.description: The contact details this member will share when an author says yes, for them to edit.

put.description: Choose what to share on a yes. The sign-in email is always shared; LinkedIn and phone are optional.
Turn email notifications on or off. Account emails are sent either way.

post.description: Revoke this session. Other signed-in sessions stay active.
Confirm a case.edu email with the 6-digit code we sent. Signs the member in.
Send a new code. Answers the same whether or not the email has an account, and at most one a minute.

get.description: Your open invites. The link itself is only shown when you make it.

schema.title: Response My Invites Auth Invites Get

post.description: Make a single-use link for an alum. It lasts 14 days; you can have 5 open at a time.
For the sign-up page: who invited you, if the link still works. Doesn't use it up.

get.description: Books on the shelf, newest first.

parameters.name: after

schema.description: The `next` value from the previous page.
schema.title: After

parameters.description: The `next` value from the previous page.

patch.description:
Change the book's title or back cover, in the member's own words. On a published book it's
live at once, and POST /interview/book/undo takes it back. 409 while proposed changes wait.

Change a chapter's title or summary. Its quotes stay. In a draft, the last version can be
restored (`has_previous`, POST /interview/book/chapters/{id}/restore).

post.description: Take the book off the shelf. No new checkouts; anything already arranged goes ahead.
Put a book that was taken down back on the shelf, in the same place as before.

get.description:
The member's interview, for resuming where they left off. If writing proposed changes failed,
a return tries once more on its own.

post.description: Start the interview and get the first question. A member with a book can't start again (409).
Write the waiting question again after a failed attempt (a 502, or `question` is null).
Answer the waiting question. The answer is saved first, then the next question is written.
Skip the waiting question and get the next one. Not on the Shape step (409).
Confirm the Librarian's playback ("Yes, that's me"), or correct it.

End the interview: stage goes to `drafting`, and the three titles are written in the background
(`step_status`). With too little material it says `needs_more` instead. In a round of adding, end
the round: the proposed changes are written in the background (`revision_status`). After a
failed write, try again.
`answer` is saved first as the answer to the waiting question, with no question after it.

Choose one of the three titles. Stage goes to `finishing`, and the book is written to match in
the background (`step_status`). After a failure, send this again.

delete.description: Remove a chapter from the draft. The blurb is rewritten for the chapters that are left.

post.description: Tell the chapter again. `rewrite_unchanged` means it couldn't be told better, and nothing changed.
Go back to the chapter's last version (`has_previous`), during the review.
Write the draft's back cover again.
Go back to the last back cover (`has_previous_blurb`), during the review.
Change to another of the three titles (`titles`), finishing the book again to match.
Put the finished book on the shelf. The interview is then done.
Add to a book on the shelf: a short new round of questions. The book doesn't change yet.

put.description: Save which changes are approved so far, as they're pressed. Nothing is applied.

post.description:
Get the back cover for the saved choices, to read before confirming (`selection_blurb_status`).
Written in the background when it has to be. Also the retry after `failed` or `stale`.

Apply the approved changes to the book on the shelf. The rest are dropped and not proposed
again. A reading answer saved meanwhile then gets its own proposal.
Propose taking a chapter out of a book on the shelf. Confirmed like any change. 409 at three chapters.
Back out of a removal the member started. Back to `done`, with nothing recorded as declined.
Take back the last applied revision (`can_undo`), until the next one is applied.

get.description: The member's own sparks waiting for their next round.

schema.title: Response List Sparks Interview Sparks Get

post.description: "I have one like this" on a chapter of someone else's book. Private: its author never knows.

get.description: The question waiting after a reading, if there is one.

schema.title: Response List Reading Questions Interview Reading Questions Get

post.description:
Answer it. From `done`, changes are written in the background (`revision_status`). During a
round it joins the round. While changes are waiting, it runs after the member decides.
Dismiss it, as quietly as a skip: never shown, never counted.

get.description: Books you've checked out, and open checkouts of your book.

post.description: Check out a book with a short message to its author.
Withdraw a checkout the author hasn't answered yet.
Say yes to a checkout of your book. Both of you now see each other's contact details.
Say no to a checkout of your book. The reader sees "this book isn't available right now".

get.description: The times each of you offered, where they overlap, and the confirmed meeting if there is one.

put.description: Replace the times you offer (up to five, 30 minutes each). Send none to take them back.
Settle on one of the offered times. Either of you can.
The video link and, if you're both nearby, a place to meet.

get.description: A calendar file for the confirmed meeting.
The conversation on an accepted checkout, oldest first, starting with the reader's checkout note.

post.description: Write in the conversation. The other person is emailed, at most once every 10 minutes.
You've seen everything in this conversation so far. Only you ever know this.

get.description: Is the API up, and is the database connected?

question_id.title: Question Id
question_id.description: The `question_id` of the question this answers.

BookCard.title: BookCard
BookCard.description: A book as it appears on the shelf.

BookEdit.title: BookEdit
BookEdit.description: The member's own words for their book's title or back cover. Plain text.

Change.title: Change
Change.description: One proposed change to a book on the shelf, which the member approves or declines.

ChapterEdit.title: ChapterEdit
ChapterEdit.description: The member's own words for a chapter's title or summary. Its quotes stay as they are.

Contact.title: Contact
Contact.description: What the other member chose to share once the author said yes (docs/trove.md §9.1).

ContactDetailsUpdate.title: ContactDetailsUpdate
ContactDetailsUpdate.description:
What a member shares once an author says yes.

The sign-in email is always shared. LinkedIn and phone are optional: send null or leave one out
to stop sharing it. Both are replaced together, so the settings form sends the whole picture.

DeleteAccountRequest.title: DeleteAccountRequest
DeleteAccountRequest.description: Deleting an account cannot be undone, so the member types their email to confirm.

answer.title: Answer
answer.description: What's in the field: saved as the waiting question's answer first.

LendingCheckout.title: LendingCheckout
LendingCheckout.description: A checkout of your book, as its author sees it.

MyBookResponse.title: MyBookResponse
MyBookResponse.description: The signed-in member's own book, as its author sees it.

NameUpdate.title: NameUpdate
NameUpdate.description: Change the name on the account. Leave out a field to keep it.

NotificationSettingsUpdate.title: NotificationSettingsUpdate
NotificationSettingsUpdate.description: The one email switch. Account emails, like the welcome message, are sent either way.

PublicBookResponse.title: PublicBookResponse
PublicBookResponse.description: A book as readers see it: the author's full name, but no contacts, copy counts or grounding quotes.

ReadingCheckout.title: ReadingCheckout
ReadingCheckout.description: A checkout as its reader sees it.

ReadingQuestionResponse.title: ReadingQuestionResponse
ReadingQuestionResponse.description: The question after a reading, for its author only.

approved.title: Approved
approved.description: The ids of the changes approved so far. Saved, not applied.

approved.title: Approved
approved.description: The ids of the changes to apply. The rest are dropped.

blurb.title: Blurb
blurb.description: "use" applies the back cover last shown for exactly this selection, from `proposed_blurb` or POST /interview/revision/blurb. "keep" leaves the old one.

question_id.title: Question Id
question_id.description: The `question_id` of the playback being answered.

correction.title: Correction
correction.description: What's different. Leave out to confirm: "Yes, that's me".

question_id.title: Question Id
question_id.description: The `question_id` of the question being skipped.

SparkResponse.title: SparkResponse
SparkResponse.description: A chapter that made this member think "I have one like this". Only they ever see it.

StaleQuestionResponse.title: StaleQuestionResponse
StaleQuestionResponse.description: The 409 when an answer or skip names a question that isn't the one waiting. Nothing was saved.

resume_pdf.title: Resume Pdf
resume_pdf.description: An optional résumé PDF, base64-encoded. The file isn't kept. Its text is deleted when the interview ends, or 30 days after the last activity, and nothing from it goes into the book.

title.title: Title
title.description: Which of the three titles, by position.
